purpose: P4 offline analysis: are the molecules the agent committed (in fix/r2/r3/r4) in the audit's known set of qualifying products, and how often do they hit the audit-best molecule?
method: Read-only: reachability.json of one run per parent to get the audit-known qualifying SMILES and the audit-best molecule; agent/task.json for each fixed-version run to get the committed deterministic_edit candidates with supported outcome. No model calls, no evaluation cache use.

observations.what: Agent never produced an out-of-set product
observations.evidence: All 8 committed deterministic_edits with outcome=supported are in the audit's known qualifying set for the parent (3/3 phenol, 2/2 aniline, 3/3 toluene). The other 2 (toluene r4) are in the audit set but at rank 6 (the lowest of 6).
observations.status: Agent's committing is correct: no hallucinated edits.

observations.what: Agent frequently finds the audit-best molecule
observations.evidence: Of 8 agent commits with supported outcome, 6 hit the audit-best: phenol 1/2, aniline 1/2, toluene 3/4.
observations.status: Compound best-hit rate 6/8 = 75%. Toluene is the most reliable.

observations.what: Toluene r4 regressed to a worse molecule
observations.evidence: fix / r2 / r3 all committed OCCCc1ccccc1 (rank 1, best delta 0.01874). r4 committed OCc1ccccc1 (rank 6, best delta 0.01092).
observations.status: r4 still goal_met, just with the lowest-qualifying molecule in the audit's 6-product set. The 0.01 threshold is the same; the agent happened to commit a different edit. No defect; just variability.

observations.what: Toluene has 6 qualifying products in the audit vs phenol's 3 and aniline's 2
observations.evidence: phenol audit qualifying: 3 SMILES; aniline: 2 SMILES; toluene: 6 SMILES.
observations.status: This is why toluene reaches goal_met more often: it has more reachable qualifying products (6 vs 3 vs 2), so the agent has more ways to hit the 0.01 threshold within the same budget.

honest_limitations: This is post-hoc analysis on the same task.json files the agent produced; it does not introduce new evidence about agent capability.
The audit-known qualifying set is itself produced by the same evaluator the agent uses, so there is no independent truth here.
We rank by the audit's delta but do not compare to any external reference or ground-truth chemistry.
8 total commits is too few for any statistical claim.
